sentences.text: The skull of this animal reaches a maximum length of one meter, with most of that span forming an elongated snout.
A long and narrow maxilla constitutes the majority of this snout, creating a distinct longirostrine appearance.
Its dentition features teeth that are generally robust and sharp.
Although its teeth were large and strong, the animal possessed fewer of them than the related species Dyrosaurus phosphaticus.
The genus was formally described in 2005 by a research team led by paleontologist Stéphane Jouve.
Four distinct specimens have been identified and described by Jouve and his colleagues.
Every described specimen originates from the Sidi Chenane phosphate mine.
The genus name honors French paleontologist Camille Arambourg for his work on fossils from Morocco's phosphate mines.
The specific name references the town of Khouribga, which lies north of the type locality.
Like other dyrosaurids, it functioned as a marine predator.
The genus authority is Jouve et al., 2005, and the type species is Arambourgisuchus khouribgaensis.
Arambourgisuchus belongs to the family Dyrosauridae.
It is classified within Dyrosauridae based on large occipital tuberosities and a supratemporal fenestra that is longer than it is wide.
Arambourgisuchus lived during the Thanetian age of the Paleocene, approximately 59 to 56 million years ago.
The lack of better material makes a correct determination of its affinities difficult.
